claims.statement: In the Prose Edda, Thor threw the hammer after the serpent and it is even said that he struck off its head at the bottom, but the narrator thinks the truth is that the Midgard-serpent still lives and lies in the ocean.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor melempar palunya mengejar ular itu dan konon memenggal kepalanya di dasar laut, tetapi sang pencerita berpendapat kebenarannya ialah Ular Midgard masih hidup dan berbaring di samudra.
claims.quote: Thor threw the hammer after it, and it is even said that he struck off his head at the bottom, but I think the truth is that the Midgard-serpent still lives and lies in the ocean.

claims.statement: In the Prose Edda, Thor gains great renown by slaying the Midgard-serpent but retreats only nine paces before falling dead, poisoned by the venom the serpent blows on him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor mendapat nama besar karena membunuh Ular Midgard, tetapi hanya mundur sembilan langkah sebelum jatuh mati, diracuni bisa yang disemburkan ular itu.
claims.quote: Thor gets great renown by slaying the Midgard-serpent, but retreats only nine paces when he falls to the earth dead, poisoned by the venom that the serpent blows on him.

claims.statement: In the Prose Edda, Thor is called Asa-Thor or Oku-Thor.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor disebut Asa-Thor atau Oku-Thor.
claims.quote: He is called Asa-Thor, or Oku-Thor.

claims.statement: Besides Old Norse Þórr, the deity occurs in Old English as Thunor, Old Frisian as Thuner, Old Saxon as Thunar, and Old High German as Donar, all ultimately from the Proto-Germanic theonym *Þun(a)raz, meaning 'Thunder'.
claims.statement_id: Selain Þórr dalam bahasa Nordik Kuno, dewa ini muncul dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno sebagai Thunor, Frisia Kuno sebagai Thuner, Saksen Kuno sebagai Thunar, dan Jerman Tinggi Kuno sebagai Donar, semuanya berasal dari nama dewa Proto-Germanik *Þun(a)raz yang berarti 'Guntur'.
claims.quote: Besides Old Norse Þórr, the deity occurs in Old English as Thunor, in Old Frisian as Thuner, in Old Saxon as Thunar, and in Old High German as Donar, all ultimately stemming from the Proto-Germanic theonym *Þun(a)raz, meaning 'Thunder'.

claims.statement: In 1962 Jack Kirby, Stan Lee, and his brother Larry Lieber created a feature in the comic Journey Into Mystery presenting Thor as a superhero; this version is portrayed as a clean-shaven blonde instead of red-haired and bearded.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1962, Jack Kirby, Stan Lee, dan saudaranya Larry Lieber menciptakan fitur dalam komik Journey Into Mystery yang menampilkan Thor sebagai pahlawan super; Thor versi ini digambarkan klimis dan berambut pirang, bukan berambut merah dan berjanggut.
claims.quote: In 1962, American comic book artist Jack Kirby, Marvel Comics editor Stan Lee, and his brother Larry Lieber created a feature in the comic book Journey Into Mystery, a series featuring Thor as a superhero. This version of Thor is portrayed as a clean-shaven blonde, instead of red-haired and bearded.

claims.statement: From 2015 to 2017 a fictionalised Thor was a supporting character in Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, a fantasy trilogy by Rick Riordan.
claims.statement_id: Dari 2015 hingga 2017, versi fiksi Thor menjadi tokoh pendukung dalam Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, trilogi novel fantasi karya Rick Riordan.
claims.quote: From 2015 to 2017, a fictionalised version of Thor was a supporting character in Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, a trilogy of fantasy novels written by American author Rick Riordan

claims.statement: In January 2020 Netflix produced Ragnarok, in which a high school student, Magne Seier, receives Thor's powers and abilities to fight the giants polluting Norway and murdering people.
claims.statement_id: Pada Januari 2020 Netflix memproduksi Ragnarok; dalam serial itu seorang siswa SMA, Magne Seier, menerima kekuatan dan kemampuan Thor untuk melawan raksasa yang mencemari Norwegia dan membunuh orang.
claims.quote: In January 2020, the streaming service Netflix produced Ragnarok. In the show, a high school student, Magne Seier, receives Thor's powers and abilities to fight the giants that are polluting Norway and murdering people.

claims.statement: Thor therefore became the Norse god of the everyman, a common-sense, no-nonsense deity anyone could relate to and everyone could depend on.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu Thor menjadi dewa Nordik bagi orang biasa: dewa yang bernalar sederhana dan tanpa basa-basi, yang dapat dipahami siapa pun dan diandalkan semua orang.
claims.quote: Thor therefore became the Norse god of the everyman; the common-sense, no-nonsense deity anyone could relate to and everyone could depend on.

claims.statement: Hades is the ancient Greek god of the dead and riches and king of the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan kekayaan serta raja alam bawah dalam agama Yunani kuno.
claims.quote: in the ancient Greek religion and mythology, is the god of the dead and riches and the King of the underworld, with which his name became synonymous.

claims.statement: Hades received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea.
claims.statement_id: Hades mendapat alam bawah, Zeus langit, dan Poseidon laut.
claims.quote: Hades received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea

claims.statement: Hades presided over funerary rites and defended the dead's right to burial.
claims.statement_id: Hades memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan layak.
claims.quote: He presided over funeral rites and defended the right of the dead to due burial.

claims.statement: Hades was also god of the earth's hidden wealth, including fertile soil and metals.
claims.statement_id: Hades juga dewa kekayaan tersembunyi di bumi, dari tanah subur hingga logam.
claims.quote: Haides was also the god of the hidden wealth of the earth, from the fertile soil with nourished the seed-grain, to the mined wealth of gold, silver and other metals.

claims.statement: Hades names both the god and the underworld considered the destination of dead souls.
claims.statement_id: Hades adalah nama dewa sekaligus nama tempat alam bawah yang dianggap tujuan akhir jiwa orang mati.
claims.quote: Hades was both the name of the ancient Greek god of the underworld (Roman name: Pluto) and the name of the shadowy place below the earth which was considered the final destination for the souls of the dead.

claims.statement: Persephone is named as Hades's wife whom he brought to the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Persephone disebut sebagai istri Hades yang dibawanya ke alam bawah.
claims.quote: The god's wife was Persephone whom he abducted to join him in the underworld

claims.statement: Hades is described as dwelling in a dark palace beneath the earth rather than on Olympus.
claims.statement_id: Hades digambarkan tinggal di istana gelap di bawah bumi, bukan di Olympus.
claims.quote: Hades was the only god not to reside on Mount Olympus, dwelling instead in a dark palace beneath the earth.

claims.statement: According to Theoi, Haides was devoured by Kronos as soon as he was born along with four siblings; Zeus later made the Titan disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them in the pit of Tartaros.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Theoi, Haides ditelan Kronos begitu lahir bersama empat saudaranya; Zeus kemudian membuat sang Titan memuntahkan mereka, dan bersama-sama mereka mengusir para dewa Titan dari langit dan mengurung mereka di jurang Tartaros.
claims.quote: Haides was devoured by Kronos (Cronus) as soon as he was born, along with four of his siblings. Zeus later caused the Titan to disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them away in the pit of Tartaros.

claims.statement: In the Iliad (Lattimore's translation), Poseidon says that when the lots were shaken he drew the grey sea, Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad (terjemahan Lattimore), Poseidon berkata bahwa ketika undi dikocok ia mendapat laut kelabu, Aides mendapat undi kabut dan kegelapan, dan Zeus mendapat langit luas.
claims.quote: I [Poseidon] when the lots were shaken drew the grey sea to live in forever; Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky, in the cloud and the bright air.

claims.statement: In Hesiod's Theogony Haides is described as strong, pitiless in heart, and dwelling under the earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides digambarkan kuat, tanpa belas kasih di hatinya, dan berdiam di bawah bumi.
claims.quote: strong Haides (Hades), pitiless in heart, who dwells under the earth

claims.statement: Haides desired a bride and asked his brother Zeus for one of his daughters; Zeus offered Persephone, daughter of Demeter, and, knowing Demeter would resist, assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.
claims.statement_id: Haides menginginkan pengantin dan memohon kepada saudaranya Zeus agar memberinya salah satu putrinya; Zeus menawarkan Persephone, putri Demeter, dan karena tahu Demeter akan menolak, ia menyetujui penculikan paksa gadis itu.
claims.quote: Haides desired a bride and petitioned his brother Zeus to grant him one of his daughters. The god offered him Persephone, the daughter of Demeter. However, knowing that the goddess would resist the marriage, he assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

claims.statement: Demeter was furious and brought a great dearth upon the earth until her daughter was returned; Zeus was forced to concede and the girl was fetched from the underworld, but since she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return to Haides for a portion of each year.
claims.statement_id: Demeter murka dan menimpakan paceklik besar ke bumi sampai putrinya dikembalikan; Zeus terpaksa mengalah dan gadis itu dijemput dari dunia bawah, tetapi karena telah mencicipi biji delima ia harus kembali kepada Haides selama sebagian tiap tahun.
claims.quote: When Demeter learned of this, she was furious and caused a great dearth to fall upon the earth until her daughter was returned. Zeus was forced to concede lest mankind perish, and the girl was fetched forth from the underworld. However, since she had tasted of the pomegranate seed, she was forced to return to him for a portion of each year.

claims.statement: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god, either as Aidoneus enthroned in the underworld holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton, the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.
claims.statement_id: Haides digambarkan sebagai dewa berjanggut gelap yang agung, entah sebagai Aidoneus yang bertakhta di dunia bawah dengan tongkat berujung burung, atau sebagai Plouton, pemberi kekayaan, yang mencurahkan kesuburan dari cornucopia.
claims.quote: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god. He was depicted as either Aidoneus, enthroned in the underworld, holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton (Pluton), the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

claims.statement: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Romawi menamainya Dis atau Pluto, bentuk Latin dari gelar Yunaninya Plouton, "Penguasa Kekayaan".
claims.quote: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades possessed a helmet that rendered the wearer invisible, and later traditions said it was a gift from the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat, dan tradisi kemudian menyebut helm itu hadiah dari para Kiklops setelah mereka dibebaskan dari Tartarus.
claims.quote: He possessed a helmet which rendered the wearer invisible (Il. v. 845), and later traditions stated that this helmet was given him as a present by the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades kept the gates of the lower world closed so that no shade could escape or return to the region of light.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides menjaga gerbang dunia bawah tetap tertutup agar tak ada arwah yang dapat lolos atau kembali ke wilayah cahaya.
claims.quote: He kept the gates of the lower world closed (whence he is called ... that no shade might be able to escape or return to the region of light.

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, his character is described as fierce and inexorable, so that of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, wataknya digambarkan garang dan tak kenal ampun sehingga di antara semua dewa ia paling dibenci manusia.
claims.quote: His character is described as fierce and inexorable, whence of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.

claims.statement: In Elis Hades had a sacred enclosure and a temple that was opened only once every year.
claims.statement_id: Di Elis Haides memiliki pelataran suci dan sebuah kuil yang hanya dibuka sekali setiap tahun.
claims.quote: In Elis he had a sacred enclosure and a temple, which was opened only once in every year

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Plato observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Plato mencatat bahwa orang lebih suka menyebutnya Pluton (pemberi kekayaan) daripada mengucapkan nama Hades atau Aides yang ditakuti.
claims.quote: Plato (Cratyl. p. 403) observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, the etymology of Hades is uncertain; some derive it from a-idein, so that it would signify "the god who makes invisible".
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, asal-usul kata Hades tidak pasti; sebagian menurunkannya dari a-idein sehingga berarti "dewa yang membuat tak terlihat".
claims.quote: The etymology of Hades is uncertain: some derive it from a-idein, whence it would signify "the god who makes invisible,"

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, in Homer Aides is always the name of the god, but later it was transferred to his house, abode or kingdom and became a name for the lower world itself.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, dalam Homeros Aides selalu nama sang dewa, tetapi kemudian dialihkan ke rumah, tempat tinggal, atau kerajaannya sehingga menjadi nama dunia bawah itu sendiri.
claims.quote: In Homer Aides is invariably the name of the god; but in later times it was transferred to his house, his abode or kingdom, so that it became a name for the lower world itself.

claims.statement: According to Theoi, the three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides, but the usual account describes them as earth-born.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Theoi, tiga dewi murka bumi kadang digambarkan sebagai putri Haides, tetapi kisah yang lazim menyebut mereka lahir dari bumi.
claims.quote: The three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides. The usual account, however, describes them as earth-born.

claims.statement: In Pseudo-Apollodorus's Bibliotheca the Kyklopes gave Zeus thunder, lightning and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Haides) and a trident for Poseidon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bibliotheca Pseudo-Apollodoros, para Kiklops memberi Zeus guntur dan petir, serta helm untuk Plouton (Haides) dan trisula untuk Poseidon.
claims.quote: In return the Kyklopes (Cyclopes) gave Zeus thunder, lightning, and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Pluton) [Haides] and a trident for Poseidon.

claims.statement: In Hesiod's Theogony, Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below as Zeus battled Typhoeus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides gemetar di tempat ia memerintah orang mati di bawah ketika Zeus bertarung melawan Typhoeus.
claims.quote: Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades was perhaps the most feared of the gods and is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades mungkin dewa yang paling ditakuti dan oleh Homeros maupun Hesiodos disebut 'tanpa belas kasih', 'menjijikkan', dan 'mengerikan'.
claims.quote: Perhaps the most feared of the gods, he is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous' Hades.

claims.statement: Even speaking his name was avoided; epithets such as Eubuleus (giving good advice) were used instead.
claims.statement_id: Bahkan menyebut namanya dihindari; sebagai gantinya dipakai gelar seperti Eubuleus (pemberi nasihat baik).
claims.quote: Indeed, even to speak his name was avoided; instead epithets were used such as Eubuleus (giving good advice).

claims.statement: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices in honour of Hades, carried out at night, with the victims' blood left to seep into the earth to reach the underworld god.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula catatan tentang praktik kurban untuk Hades yang dilakukan malam hari dengan darah korban dibiarkan meresap ke tanah agar sampai ke dewa dunia bawah.
claims.quote: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices made in honour of Hades, carried out at night and where the blood of victims was left to seep down into the earth to reach the underworld god.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades had a helmet made by Hephaistos that rendered the wearer invisible; it was used by Athena when she fought Ares in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for Medusa's head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades memiliki helm buatan Hephaistos yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; helm itu dipakai Athena saat melawan Ares dalam Iliad dan oleh Perseus dalam perburuan kepala Medusa.
claims.quote: The god also had a helmet made by Hephaistos which rendered the wearer invisible, and it was this helmet that was used by Athena when she fought Ares in Homer's account of the Trojan War in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for the head of Medusa.

claims.statement: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi, Hades jatuh cinta pada Persephone, putri Zeus dan Demeter, dan menculiknya untuk tinggal bersamanya.
claims.quote: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

claims.statement: Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed so that she could only return to the living for half of the year; the myth was perhaps symbolic of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.
claims.statement_id: Hades menipu gadis itu agar memakan biji delima sehingga ia hanya dapat kembali kepada yang hidup selama setengah tahun; mitos ini mungkin melambangkan siklus hidup dan mati, penanaman dan panen.
claims.quote: However, Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed and therefore she could only return to the living for half of the year. This myth was symbolic perhaps of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

claims.statement: When Hermes discovered this he demanded that Persephone be returned to Demeter, and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades she could return to the upper world.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Hermes mengetahuinya, ia menuntut Persephone dikembalikan kepada Demeter dan diputuskan bahwa jika ia belum makan apa pun dari Hades, ia boleh kembali ke dunia atas.
claims.quote: When Hermes discovered this, he demanded Persephone be returned to Demeter and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades, she could return to the upper world.

claims.statement: In Archaic and Classical Greek art Hades is most often a mature bearded man holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia, symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth that comes from the ground.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni Yunani Arkais dan Klasik, Hades paling sering digambarkan sebagai pria dewasa berjanggut yang memegang tongkat, tombak bermata dua, bejana libasi, atau cornucopia, lambang kekayaan mineral dan nabati dari tanah.
claims.quote: In Archaic and Classical Greek art, Hades is most often represented as a more mature man, bearded and holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia - symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth which comes from the ground.

claims.statement: On occasion he is shown seated on an ebony throne or riding a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia digambarkan duduk di singgasana eboni atau menunggang kereta yang ditarik kuda hitam, sering dengan Persephone di sisinya.
claims.quote: On occasion he is seated on an ebony throne or rides a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

claims.statement: Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx, where the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades, guarded by Kerberos, a ferocious three-headed dog (fifty-headed according to Hesiod) who kept souls in rather than others out.
claims.statement_id: Hermes dipercaya menuntun jiwa ke Sungai Styx di dunia bawah, tempat juru perahu tua Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang Hades, yang dijaga Kerberos, anjing ganas berkepala tiga (atau lima puluh menurut Hesiodos) yang menjaga agar jiwa tetap di dalam.
claims.quote: The god Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx in the underworld, at which point the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades where Kerberos - the ferocious three-headed dog (or fifty-headed according to Hesiod) with serpents coming out of its body - stood guard to keep souls in rather than to keep others out.

claims.statement: To pay Charon, bereaved families put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (the traditional Greek coin was the low-value obol); the unburied or those unable to pay were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membayar Charon, keluarga yang berduka menaruh koin di mulut jenazah (bagi orang Yunani koin tradisionalnya obol bernilai rendah); orang yang tak dikubur atau tak mampu membayar dihukum mengembara di bumi sebagai hantu.
claims.quote: It was for payment to Charon that bereaved family members put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (for Greeks the traditional coin was the low-value obol). The unburied or those without the means to pay the boatman were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

claims.statement: Traditionally the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.
claims.statement_id: Secara tradisional, tiga hakim jiwa adalah Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos, yang terkenal karena hidup terhormat.
claims.quote: Traditionally, the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

claims.statement: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe, which made them forget all bad things, and then to the idyllic Elysian Fields.
claims.statement_id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup sangat baik lebih dulu diajak minum air Sungai Lethe yang membuat mereka melupakan semua hal buruk, lalu dibawa ke Padang Elysium yang indah.
claims.quote: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe which made them forget all bad things, and then they were taken to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

claims.statement: Souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to be punished for their misdeeds.
claims.statement_id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup buruk diserahkan kepada para Furia dan dibawa ke Tartarus, tingkat terendah Hades, untuk menerima hukuman atas perbuatan mereka.
claims.quote: Those souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to receive punishment for their misdeeds.

claims.statement: Though fearful to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes: Hercules to capture Kerberos in his last labour, Odysseus to seek Tiresias's advice, Orpheus to find Eurydice, and Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that Peirithoos might marry her.
claims.statement_id: Meski menakutkan bagi yang hidup, Hades dikunjungi beberapa pahlawan: Hercules untuk menangkap Kerberos pada pekerjaan kedua belasnya, Odiseus untuk meminta nasihat Tiresias, Orpheus untuk mencari Eurydice, dan Theseus serta Peirithoos untuk menculik Persephone agar dinikahi Peirithoos.
claims.quote: Although a fearful place to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes in the course of their various adventures, including Hercules to capture Kerberos in the last of his twelve labours, by Odysseus to seek the advice of wise Tiresias, by Orpheus to find Eurydice, and by Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that she might marry the latter.

claims.statement: The last two heroes were less fortunate: Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied them to two rocks in other accounts), and only Theseus later escaped when Hercules released him.
claims.statement_id: Kedua pahlawan terakhir itu kurang beruntung karena Hades memenjarakan mereka di dua singgasana (atau mengikat mereka pada dua batu menurut kisah lain), dan hanya Theseus yang kemudian lolos ketika Hercules membebaskannya.
claims.quote: These last two heroes were, however, less fortunate than the others in that Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied to two rocks in other accounts) and only Theseus would later escape from the underworld when Hercules released him.

claims.statement: After the Olympian gods overthrew first the Titans and then the Giants, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.
claims.statement_id: Setelah para dewa Olimpus menggulingkan Titan lalu Raksasa, Hades mengundi dengan saudara-saudaranya, Zeus dan Poseidon, untuk menentukan bagian dunia yang akan diperintah masing-masing.
claims.quote: Following the overthrow of first the Titans and then the Giants by the Olympian gods, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

claims.statement: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul nama Hades tidak pasti, tetapi sejak zaman kuno umumnya dianggap berarti "yang tak terlihat".
claims.quote: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

claims.statement: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus with Hades, merging them all into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton.
claims.statement_id: Para mitograf zaman Romawi akhirnya menyamakan dewa Etruria Aita serta dewa Romawi Dis Pater dan Orcus dengan Hades dan menggabungkan semuanya menjadi Pluto, Latinisasi dari Plouton.
claims.quote: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita, and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus, with Hades, and merged all these figures into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton

claims.statement: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.
claims.statement_id: Hades adalah putra sulung Kronos dan Rhea, meski itu juga membuatnya putra terakhir yang dimuntahkan ayahnya.
claims.quote: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

claims.statement: Martin Litchfield West instead argues for an original meaning of "the one who presides over meeting up", from the universality of death.
claims.statement_id: Martin Litchfield West mengusulkan makna asli "yang memimpin pertemuan" yang berasal dari universalitas kematian.
claims.quote: Martin Litchfield West argues instead for an original meaning of "the one who presides over meeting up" from the universality of death.

claims.statement: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, he is hence called the infernal Zeus (Zeus katachthonios) or the king of the shades.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, karena itu ia disebut Zeus dunia bawah (Zeus katachthonios) atau raja para arwah.
claims.quote: Hence he is called the infernal Zeus (Zeus katachthonios), or the king of the shades
